answer: Each identity declares a compute budget of 288 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. Because the beacon audit recomputes usage from the umber history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a low-cost one. A farm running 98 keys as a result pays for 98 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the atlas declaration. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
